records.Title: System voltage
records.Explanation: Nominal line-to-line voltage of the MV network.
records.How app uses it: Used to calculate current, voltage drop, charging current and select a compatible cable voltage designation.
records.Worked example: For an 11 kV network, use 11 kV and select a cable voltage designation accepted by the utility and insulation-coordination study.
records.Warning: Do not select cable voltage class from nominal voltage alone; confirm system earthing, Um, overvoltage duty and TNB/project requirements.
records.Reference table: Network / Common Malaysia use | 6.6 kV / Selected Johor/Perak or private systems | 11 kV / Common distribution | 22 kV / Selected Johor/Perak | 33 kV / Higher-capacity distribution

records.Title: Load / transformer capacity
records.Explanation: Apparent power used to derive three-phase current.
records.How app uses it: I = S / (√3 × V). In cable design, the app applies demand and derating separately.
records.Worked example: 1,000 kVA at 11 kV gives approximately 52.5 A.
records.Warning: Confirm whether the entered value is connected load, maximum demand, transformer rating or actual measured demand.
records.Reference table: Input type / Use | kVA / Direct apparent power | kW / Requires power factor and efficiency | A / Direct design current

records.Title: Power factor
records.Explanation: Ratio of real power to apparent power.
records.How app uses it: Affects current when input is kW and affects voltage-drop resistance/reactance components.
records.Worked example: 1,000 kW at PF 0.90 requires about 1,111 kVA before efficiency adjustment.
records.Warning: Do not assume unity PF for motors or industrial loads. TNB may impose minimum PF requirements.
records.Reference table: Typical load / Preliminary PF | Motors / mixed industrial / 0.80–0.90 | Corrected industrial / 0.90–0.95 | Power electronics / Use measured/fundamental PF

records.Title: Installation method
records.Explanation: Physical arrangement controlling cable heat dissipation.
records.How app uses it: Selects the reference ampacity basis before ambient, soil and grouping factors.
records.Worked example: A directly buried cable and the same cable in a duct can have different current ratings.
records.Warning: Use exact manufacturer/IEC 60287 installation data for final design.
records.Reference table: Method / Reference basis | Air — trefoil / Single-core cables touching | Air — flat / Single-core cables in flat formation | Direct buried / Cable in soil | Underground duct / Cable in duct/pipe

records.Title: Soil thermal resistivity
records.Explanation: Resistance of surrounding soil to heat flow, expressed in K·m/W.
records.How app uses it: The app applies a conservative correction to direct-buried and duct reference ampacity.
records.Worked example: A change from 1.2 to 2.5 K·m/W can materially reduce permissible current.
records.Warning: Site-specific thermal-resistivity testing is preferred for heavily loaded MV routes.
records.Reference table: Condition / Indicative value | Moist controlled backfill / 0.8–1.2 K·m/W | Typical design assumption / 1.2–1.5 K·m/W | Dry/high-resistivity soil / 2.0–2.5+ K·m/W

records.Title: Fault current
records.Explanation: Prospective RMS short-circuit current through the cable conductor or screen.
records.How app uses it: Compared with adiabatic conductor and screen withstand for the selected clearing time.
records.Worked example: 20 kA for 1 s requires substantially less area than 20 kA for 3 s.
records.Warning: Use the maximum credible fault current at the cable location and actual protection clearing time.
records.Reference table: TNB voltage / Published equipment duty | 11 kV / 20 kA, 3 s | 22 kV / 20 kA, 3 s | 33 kV / 25 kA, 3 s

records.Title: Fault clearing time
records.Explanation: Total time from fault inception to interruption.
records.How app uses it: Adiabatic withstand varies inversely with √t.
records.Worked example: A 1-second rating cannot automatically be treated as a 3-second rating.
records.Warning: Include relay, breaker and grading time. Verify backup-clearing duty.
records.Reference table: Assessment / Typical source | Primary clearing / Relay + breaker curve | Backup clearing / Upstream grading study | Utility duty / TNB/project specification

records.Title: Screen bonding
records.Explanation: How metallic screens/sheaths are earthed and interconnected.
records.How app uses it: Affects sheath losses, induced voltage and zero-sequence behavior.
records.Worked example: Both-end bonding can create circulating current; single-point bonding can create standing voltage.
records.Warning: A full sheath-voltage and bonding study may be required for long/high-current single-core circuits.
records.Reference table: Method / Use | Both-end bonded / Common short routes; check losses | Single-point bonded / Eliminates circulating current; check voltage | Cross-bonded / Long routes; specialist design

records.Title: Transformer impedance
records.Explanation: Nameplate percentage impedance at rated current.
records.How app uses it: Used for approximate transformer-limited LV fault current and voltage regulation.
records.Worked example: 1,000 kVA, 415 V, 6% impedance gives approximately 23.2 kA at the LV terminals when upstream impedance is neglected.
records.Warning: Use actual guaranteed impedance and tolerances for final short-circuit calculation.
records.Reference table: Rating / Preliminary reference only | ≤500 kVA / Around 4% | 750–1000 kVA / Around 5% | ≥1250 kVA / Around 6%

records.Title: Transformer loading
records.Explanation: Demand divided by transformer rating.
records.How app uses it: The app recommends the next standard rating after demand, growth, redundancy and project margins.
records.Worked example: 900 kVA demand on a 1,000 kVA transformer is 90% loading before future growth.
records.Warning: Continuous loading target depends on redundancy, ambient, harmonics, cooling and utility/project requirements.
records.Reference table: Design approach / Typical intent | Normal single transformer / Allow project growth margin | N+1 arrangement / Check outage loading | High harmonics / Consider derating/K-factor study

records.Title: Vector group
records.Explanation: Winding connection and phase displacement.
records.How app uses it: Used as a compatibility and parallel-operation attribute.
records.Worked example: Dyn11 is common for MV/LV distribution, but project and utility requirements govern.
records.Warning: Transformers operated in parallel must have compatible ratio, vector group, impedance and tap position.
records.Reference table: Example / Meaning | Dyn11 / HV delta, LV star with neutral, clock 11 | YNyn0 / Both star with neutrals; zero displacement | Custom / Verify system study

records.Title: Voltage drop
records.Explanation: Reduction in receiving-end voltage caused by cable impedance.
records.How app uses it: Calculated using R cosφ + X sinφ for a balanced three-phase circuit.
records.Worked example: At MV, reactance can be significant, especially for long routes.
records.Warning: The acceptable limit is project- and system-study-specific; do not blindly use LV limits.
records.Source / basis: IEC engineering method; TNB steady-state voltage criteria.
records.Reference table: Use / Preliminary guide | Internal feeder / Project criterion, often 1–3% | Utility connection / Coordinate with TNB ±5% network criterion | Motor starting / Separate transient study

records.Title: Cable charging current
records.Explanation: Capacitive current drawn by an energised cable even with no load.
records.How app uses it: Calculated from frequency, phase voltage, capacitance and route length.
records.Worked example: Long 33 kV cables can contribute significant MVAr and affect protection/earthing.
records.Warning: Use manufacturer capacitance for final calculation.
records.Reference table: Route / Action | Short industrial feeder / Usually small but calculate | Long 22/33 kV route / Review reactive power/protection | Export cable / Specialist cable-system study

records.Title: Brand filter
records.Explanation: Limits lookup and recommendation to the selected manufacturer family.
records.How app uses it: The app retains separate manufacturer-family and engineering-reference status.
records.Worked example: Selecting TCI shows TCI-labelled product families, but final ratings still require the exact TCI catalogue/datasheet.
records.Warning: Brand selection does not mean TNB approval or current product availability.
records.Reference table: Selection / Use | Any brand / Engineering comparison across controlled records | Named brand / Limit results to that manufacturer family

records.Title: Data verification status
records.Explanation: Shows whether a value is manufacturer-verified, standards-derived or preliminary.
records.How app uses it: The status is printed in results and reports to prevent generic values being mistaken for guaranteed product data.
records.Worked example: FAMILY VERIFIED / ENGINEERING REFERENCE means the product family exists, while electrical ratings require exact catalogue verification.
records.Warning: Do not issue procurement specifications from preliminary records without datasheet confirmation.
records.Reference table: Status / Meaning | Manufacturer verified / Exact catalogue/nameplate value captured | Engineering reference / Calculated or representative design value | Verify / Project or manufacturer confirmation required

records.Title: Conductor material
records.Explanation: Select copper or aluminium conductor. Material changes resistance, short-circuit coefficient, weight, termination practice and often the available catalogue sizes.
records.How app uses it: The cable engine filters the database by material and applies the corresponding adiabatic coefficient.
records.Worked example: A 240 mm² copper XLPE conductor has a higher 1 s thermal withstand than a 240 mm² aluminium conductor because the applied k coefficient is higher.
records.Warning: Confirm lug material, bimetallic interfaces, jointing system and manufacturer construction.
records.Source / basis: IEC 60949 adiabatic principles; IEC 60228 conductor construction; manufacturer data.
records.Reference table: Material / Typical app treatment | Copper / Lower resistance and k = 143 reference for XLPE screening | Aluminium / Larger area often required; k = 94 reference for XLPE screening

records.Title: Number of cable cores
records.Explanation: MV circuits commonly use three single-core cables or one three-core cable. Construction affects armour, screen bonding, reactance, installation and jointing.
records.How app uses it: The selected core arrangement filters records and determines the applicable formation options.
records.Worked example: A high-current 33 kV feeder may use three single-core cables in trefoil, while a shorter lower-current 11 kV feeder may use one three-core armoured cable.
records.Warning: Do not apply magnetic steel wire armour around a single-core AC cable unless the manufacturer explicitly provides a suitable non-magnetic construction.
records.Source / basis: IEC 60502-2 cable construction and manufacturer installation instructions.
records.Reference table: Arrangement / Common consideration | 1 Core / Trefoil/flat formation and screen bonding assessment | 3 Core / Integrated three-phase construction; generally SWA where armoured

records.Title: Cable family
records.Explanation: A manufacturer family groups constructions with common voltage class, insulation, screen, armour, sheath and intended installation.
records.How app uses it: The family filter prevents the engine from mixing incompatible constructions within one comparison.
records.Worked example: Selecting an LSZH armoured family limits candidates to low-smoke outer-sheath constructions.
records.Warning: A family name confirms public product scope only unless the exact catalogue row is marked manufacturer verified.
records.Source / basis: Official manufacturer product pages and controlled source register.
records.Reference table: Family attribute / Examples | Insulation / XLPE or EPR | Armour / AWA, SWA or unarmoured | Sheath / PVC, PE/MDPE or LSZH

records.Title: Cable formation
records.Explanation: Single-core cables may be installed in trefoil or flat formation. Formation changes mutual reactance, magnetic field distribution, sheath losses and heat dissipation.
records.How app uses it: The app uses the selected formation to choose a representative reactance value for voltage-drop screening.
records.Worked example: Trefoil generally provides more symmetrical phase spacing than flat formation.
records.Warning: Ampacity must ultimately follow the actual spacing, bonding and installation geometry in the manufacturer/IEC 60287 study.
records.Source / basis: IEC 60287 series and manufacturer installation data.
records.Reference table: Formation / Typical use | Trefoil / Compact three-phase grouping | Flat / Tray, trench or spaced installation

records.Title: Parallel cable runs
records.Explanation: Parallel runs increase total current capacity when one cable per phase is insufficient.
records.How app uses it: The app divides current equally between runs and multiplies total derated ampacity, screen area and charging capacitance.
records.Worked example: Two equal 240 mm² runs per phase are screened as sharing half the phase current each.
records.Warning: Equal sharing requires equal conductor length, size, material, formation, termination and impedance.
records.Source / basis: IEC installation principles and good engineering practice.
records.Reference table: Runs per phase / Required check | 1 / Single circuit calculation | 2 or more / Equal sharing, grouping and circulating-current verification

records.Title: Ambient or soil temperature
records.Explanation: Cable ampacity decreases as the surrounding temperature approaches the conductor maximum operating temperature.
records.How app uses it: The app applies a square-root temperature correction referenced to 30 °C in air or 25 °C in soil for preliminary screening.
records.Worked example: An air-installed XLPE cable at 45 °C receives a lower correction factor than the same cable at 30 °C.
records.Warning: Use the project design temperature and the exact manufacturer/standard correction table for final issue.
records.Source / basis: IEC 60287 thermal principles and IEC 60364-style correction concepts used only as preliminary screening.
records.Reference table: Environment / App reference | Air / 30 °C | Soil / 25 °C

records.Title: Transformer type
records.Explanation: Oil-immersed and dry-type transformers have different cooling, enclosure, fire, indoor-room, loss and maintenance considerations.
records.How app uses it: The app filters the transformer database by the selected construction.
records.Worked example: A dry-type transformer may be preferred indoors where oil containment is undesirable, subject to ventilation and fire strategy.
records.Warning: Final selection must consider authority, insurer, fire code, room ventilation, noise and environmental requirements.
records.Reference table: Type / Typical cooling | Oil Immersed / ONAN / ONAF | Dry Type / AN / AF

records.Title: Demand factor
records.Explanation: Demand factor represents the fraction of connected load expected to operate simultaneously at the design maximum demand.
records.How app uses it: The app multiplies connected-load kVA by the entered factor before growth and special allowances.
records.Worked example: 800 kW connected load at 0.9 demand factor contributes 720 kW before power-factor and efficiency conversion.
records.Warning: Base the factor on measured profiles, equipment duty, client criteria or an approved load schedule—not a generic guess.
records.Source / basis: Project load assessment and utility maximum-demand practice.
records.Reference table: Factor / Interpretation | 1.00 / All connected load assumed coincident | 0.80 / 80% coincident design demand | <0.60 / Requires strong project evidence

records.Title: Future load growth
records.Explanation: Growth allowance reserves capacity for credible future expansion during the project planning horizon.
records.How app uses it: The app increases calculated base demand by the entered percentage.
records.Worked example: A 900 kVA base demand with 15% growth becomes 1,035 kVA before other allowances.
records.Warning: Avoid double-counting growth already included in the connected-load schedule.
records.Source / basis: Project planning criteria and client-approved expansion forecast.
records.Reference table: Growth / Planning interpretation | 0% / No reserved expansion | 10–20% / Common preliminary allowance | >25% / Confirm staged or master-plan basis

records.Title: Harmonic allowance
records.Explanation: Nonlinear loads increase RMS current and transformer/cable losses and may require derating or harmonic-rated equipment.
records.How app uses it: The app applies a transparent multiplicative allowance to transformer design demand in professional mode.
records.Worked example: A factor of 1.10 adds 10% capacity allowance before standard rating selection.
records.Warning: This is not a harmonic load-flow or K-factor calculation. Obtain harmonic spectra and perform a dedicated study for material nonlinear loads.
records.Source / basis: IEC 60076 loading/loss concepts and project harmonic study.
records.Reference table: Factor / Use | 1.00 / No additional allowance | 1.05–1.15 / Preliminary nonlinear-load allowance | Study required / High VFD/UPS/data-centre concentration

records.Title: Transformer redundancy
records.Explanation: Redundancy defines whether one transformer or an N+1 arrangement must support the design demand.
records.How app uses it: For two-unit N+1 mode, the app checks normal shared loading and one-unit-outage loading.
records.Worked example: Two 1,000 kVA units carrying 1,200 kVA operate at 60% each normally and 120% on the remaining unit during outage.
records.Warning: Emergency loading duration, thermal history, switching, protection and maintenance philosophy require project-specific confirmation.
records.Source / basis: IEC 60076 loading principles and client reliability criteria.
records.Reference table: Mode / Sizing requirement | Single unit / One unit carries design demand | N+1 — two units / Each unit screened against full outage demand

records.Title: Transformer cooling class
records.Explanation: Cooling class describes how heat is transferred from transformer windings and insulation to the environment.
records.How app uses it: The database displays the representative cooling class for the selected transformer type.
records.Worked example: ONAN means oil natural circulation and air natural cooling; AN means air natural cooling for dry type.
records.Warning: Forced cooling ratings are valid only with the specified fans, controls and duty.
records.Source / basis: IEC 60076 series cooling designations and manufacturer data.
records.Reference table: Code / Meaning | ONAN / Oil natural / air natural | ONAF / Oil natural / air forced | AN / Air natural dry type | AF / Air forced dry type

records.Title: Protection profile
records.Explanation: A controlled engineering preset that governs screening margins and automatic preference logic.
records.How app uses it: The app uses the selected profile to choose conservative VCB/ACB/CT margins and enhanced relay recommendations.
records.Worked example: The critical-facility profile prefers a VCB and increased duty margin even for a smaller transformer.
records.Warning: A profile is not a utility approval or final protection philosophy.
records.Reference table: Profile / Intended use | Malaysia / IEC preliminary / Ordinary preliminary design | Critical facility / Conservative continuity and protection preference

records.Title: MV protection strategy
records.Explanation: Preferred primary protection method: automatic risk-based selection, VCB or switch-fuse.
records.How app uses it: Automatic mode assesses transformer rating, number of units, criticality, enhanced scheme and available fuse screening.
records.Worked example: A single non-critical 500 kVA transformer may be screened for switch-fuse; parallel or critical units prefer VCB.
records.Warning: Do not use a universal kVA boundary as a final rule. Verify utility and fuse-manufacturer coordination.
records.Reference table: Strategy / Meaning | Auto / Risk-based preliminary preference | VCB / Numerical relay and breaker | Switch-fuse / Manufacturer-coordinated fuse links

records.Title: MV switchgear fault duty
records.Explanation: Maximum prospective short-circuit current and duration that the MV breaker and switchgear must withstand and interrupt.
records.How app uses it: The app selects the next rating envelope not below the entered maximum fault level and duration.
records.Worked example: A 20 kA system requires a VCB and switchboard rated at least 20 kA for the specified duration.
records.Warning: Use the maximum and minimum utility fault cases, actual relay clearing and backup duration.
records.Reference table: Common screening ratings / kA | 20 | 25 | 31.5 | 40 | 50

records.Title: VCB automatic selection
records.Explanation: Selection of the required MV circuit-breaker voltage, continuous-current, breaking and short-time withstand envelope.
records.How app uses it: The app rounds voltage, current and fault duty up to controlled rating series.
records.Worked example: An 11 kV, 20 kA feeder normally screens to a 12 kV VCB with at least 20 kA duty and 630 A continuous current.
records.Warning: Output is a required rating envelope, not an exact purchasable model. Verify panel type tests and manufacturer data.
records.Reference table: Parameter / Check | Rated voltage / ≥ Um | Continuous current / ≥ design current and panel rating | Breaking current / ≥ maximum fault | Short-time withstand / ≥ thermal duty

records.Title: MV transformer-fuse screening
records.Explanation: Preliminary current-limiting fuse-link current screening for a transformer switch-fuse arrangement.
records.How app uses it: The app estimates a fuse-current starting point and chooses the next controlled rating.
records.Worked example: A transformer primary current of 52.5 A may screen to a higher fuse rating after applying an inrush allowance.
records.Warning: Final selection requires the exact transformer inrush, fuse time-current curve, minimum melting, maximum clearing and switch-fuse compatibility.
records.Reference table: Required check / Evidence | Inrush withstand / Transformer energisation curve | Fault clearing / Fuse curve | Low-current interruption / Fuse type | Striker / Switch trip compatibility

records.Title: Protection CT selection
records.Explanation: Preliminary CT primary ratio and protection-core requirements for relay measurement.
records.How app uses it: The app selects a standard ratio so transformer full-load current is normally below the profile utilisation target.
records.Worked example: 52.5 A at an 80% target gives 65.6 A; the next standard ratio may be 75/1 A.
records.Warning: Differential and REF protection require class, burden, lead resistance, ALF and saturation/knee-point calculations.
records.Reference table: Application / Preliminary class | OC/EF / 5P20 or project specification | Differential/REF / PX/PS or manufacturer-specified class | Metering / Separate metering core

records.Title: Protection relay functions
records.Explanation: ANSI/IEC protection elements recommended for the selected transformer scheme.
records.How app uses it: The app assigns core functions and conditionally adds differential, REF, breaker-failure or supervision functions.
records.Worked example: A standard VCB feeder may receive 50/51, 50N/51N, 49 and 74TCS; a critical large transformer may add 87T and 64REF.
records.Warning: Final pickup, curve, delay and trip matrix require a coordination study and utility approval.
records.Reference table: Function / Purpose | 50/51 / Phase overcurrent | 50N/51N / Earth fault | 49 / Thermal | 87T / Differential | 64REF / Restricted earth fault

records.Title: LV ACB automatic selection
records.Explanation: Selection of ACB frame, sensor, breaking capacity, short-time withstand and pole arrangement.
records.How app uses it: The app rounds the transformer LV full-load current and prospective fault duty up to controlled ACB rating series.
records.Worked example: A 1,000 kVA, 415 V transformer has about 1,391 A full-load current and may screen to a 1,600 A frame.
records.Warning: Frame rating is not the long-time setting. Verify Icu, Ics, Icw, busbar/cable capacity and discrimination at the actual voltage.
records.Reference table: Item / Meaning | In / Frame or rated current | Ir / Long-time pickup | Isd / Short-time pickup | Ii / Instantaneous pickup | Ig / Ground-fault pickup

records.Title: ACB LSIG settings
records.Explanation: Preliminary long-time, short-time, instantaneous and ground-fault setting starting points.
records.How app uses it: The app provides transparent starting values and disables instantaneous where transformer inrush/fault separation is inadequate.
records.Worked example: Ir may start near transformer full-load current, while Isd and delays are coordinated with outgoing devices.
records.Warning: Never issue final settings without exact trip-unit ranges, transformer inrush, fault study and manufacturer discrimination tables.
records.Source / basis: IEC 60947-2; manufacturer trip-unit and selectivity documentation.
records.Reference table: Element / Preliminary role | L / Overload | S / Delayed short circuit | I / High-current instantaneous | G / Ground fault

records.Title: Transformer internal protection
records.Explanation: Mechanical and thermal protective devices fitted to oil-immersed or dry-type transformers.
records.How app uses it: The app recommends items based on transformer construction and enhanced protection selection.
records.Worked example: An oil transformer may require temperature, pressure and gas-actuated protection; dry type uses winding-temperature monitoring.
records.Warning: Actual available contacts, alarm/trip stages and lockout logic must follow the manufacturer schematic and project cause-and-effect matrix.
records.Reference table: Type / Typical items | Oil immersed / Buchholz, pressure relief, OTI, WTI, oil level | Dry type / Temperature controller, fans, ventilation

records.Title: Protection status
records.Explanation: Confidence label for each automatic selection.
records.How app uses it: PASS means entered rating checks pass; VERIFY means engineering/product confirmation remains; FAIL means insufficient duty; NOT ASSESSED means missing input.
records.Worked example: A 25 kA ACB on a calculated 30 kA bus is FAIL. A 50 kA ACB may remain VERIFY pending Ics/Icw and selectivity.
records.Warning: VERIFY is not approval. The app intentionally does not claim final discrimination without curves.
records.Reference table: Status / Meaning | PASS / Entered numerical checks pass | VERIFY / Plausible but confirmation required | FAIL / Inadequate | NOT ASSESSED / Missing/invalid input
